mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over 3 months indicates a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods following a 10% drop in HOUST (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods following a 0.5% increase in UNRATE (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over 3 months signals a strengthening supply side, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods following a 2% increase in INDPRO (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over 3 months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increasing RSAFS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which boosts consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods meeting the trigger conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure in a high-rate environment, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods meeting the trigger conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by less than 1% over a quarter and housing starts (HOUST) drop by more than 5% in the same period, it signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 1% and HOUST drops > 5% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods meeting the trigger conditions (t-test p > 0.05).
